Meta推出了全新的Muse助手，标志着该公司首次真正进军AI生产力工具领域。该公司表示，其AI智能体可以通过协助网购、处理邮件、规划行程等任务，“分担你的杂务”。我决定上手体验这款新工具并看看它的表现——尤其是考虑到这家公司以往更看重娱乐而非生产力。尽管该AI助手的运行大体符合我的预期，但它自主收集的关于我的海量信息令人不安，这在很大程度上冲淡了我的使用体验。
Muse是通过基于云的虚拟电脑执行操作的，我分配给它的首批任务之一就是整理我的Gmail收件箱，并删除我不需要的邮件。这需要我将Muse与我的Google账户关联，并授权其访问、阅读和删除邮件。这个过程在移动端并不顺利；Google登录页面不断出现故障，总是把我跳回Muse网站而非App。最终我在笔记本电脑上成功运行了它，它删除了数千封推广邮件和更新通知。鉴于Meta多年来在隐私方面的过往记录，授权Muse查看我的全部邮件让我感到心里没底。
Meta表示，Muse的设计仅与第三方应用交换“为用户服务所必需”的数据。该公司还声称不会与广告商分享你的信息。我依然心存不安，但还是硬着头皮将我的亚马逊账户绑定到了Muse。我让该AI智能体根据指定的尺码、款式和颜色为我挑选运动上衣。在下单前，Muse注意到我购物车里还有其他商品，并询问我是否需要将其移除。这份体贴让我颇为惊喜。待我确认购买后，它便顺利地只下单购买了背心。
换个方向，我又测试了Muse的其他一些功能，它能生成类似于Gemini Notebook的AI播客、创建图像和视频，以及开发被称为“工件”（artifacts）的交互式网页或文档。当我请求生成“穿红裤子的卡通老鼠”和“戴红帽子、穿蓝背带裤、留棕色头发和胡子的卡通男子”时，Muse拒绝了我的请求。
然而，当被要求生成带有苹果（Apple）标志设备的发布会视频和多张图片时，它却毫不犹豫地照办了。在其中一张图片中，Muse生成了一款看似折叠屏iPhone的设备、一块Apple Watch和一副AirPods。每台设备都立在带有苹果标志的支架上，一名主讲人站在印满辨识度极高苹果咬痕标志的背景板前。假iPhone上甚至还带有苹果的原生应用图标，不过它出现了幻觉，把App Store命名为“照片”，同时把地图、音乐和真正的照片应用都标注为“日历”（Calender）。不过，Muse拒绝生成“苹果CEO”的图像。
接下来事情变得诡异起来。我点击进入“动态”（Feed）标签页，Muse可以在那里根据文本提示词生成某种新闻流。我提交了Meta默认包含的提示词：“为我生成一个符合我兴趣的动态流。保持语气清晰直接。确保易于速读。尽量避免标题党。”它返回了几条AI生成的时事摘要，包括关于苹果iPhone Duo发布会的简讯、袭击加州海岸的危险巨浪，以及在伊朗战争中被摧毁的油轮。该应用还列出了几条来自我当前探亲所在州的新闻报道，Muse承认这些信息是从我亚马逊订单上的送货地址中提取的。
我顺藤摸瓜继续深入，询问Muse根据我注册使用该AI智能体时关联的Instagram和Facebook账户，它还了解我的哪些信息。它滔滔不绝地报出了我非常具体的兴趣，从动漫、CrossFit到拉布拉多寻回犬、佛罗里达野生动物以及90年代/2000年代的怀旧情结——其中很多正是频繁出现在我的Instagram Reels推荐流中的话题。
就像我测试过的其他一些智能体（agentic）AI工具一样，Muse在执行低风险任务方面表现不错。我也很喜欢它能生成一份动态的“灵感”（ideas）清单，针对如何使用该工具提供个性化建议，例如提供产品的横向对比、查找并取消被遗忘的订阅，以及跟进下一批宝可梦卡牌的发售。Muse还会根据你与AI智能体的对话，维护一份待完成的“目标”（goals）动态清单。
Muse确实兑现了在后台处理日常繁琐杂务的承诺，但它从连我都无从得知的来源搜集到的个人细节之详尽，足以让我对允许Muse翻阅私人邮件和处理我的信用卡感到惴惴不安。这种程度的疑虑，将成为Meta真正需要克服的障碍。

aiStories.fullContent:
Biomolecular structure prediction is now often run at proteome scale, where the goal is to move an entire worklist through the pipeline efficiently.

NVIDIA BioNeMo Inference Runtime (BioIR) helps accelerate supported biomolecular structure-prediction models on NVIDIA GPUs while keeping the familiar PyTorch workflow. It uses optimized kernels and, where applicable, CUDA Graphs to speed model execution. For large batches of independent inputs, Ray can run a complete model replica on each GPU in a single node to increase overall throughput.

BioIR has also been used in real proteome-scale work, including the recent expansion of the AlphaFold Database (AFDB), accelerating the generation of protein-complex structures across 4,777 proteomes, about 31 million candidate complexes in total, with 1.81 million released as high-confidence predictions.

You can use it in two ways (see Figure 1, below):

This tutorial walks through BioIR’s end-to-end processor, from input preparation to GPU inference and PDB or mmCIF output, and shows how to track structures per hour and resource efficiency.

The wheel contains precompiled CUBINs, so runtime use does not require nvcc, CUDA source, CMake, or the CUDA toolkit.

In the following, we demonstrate the end-to-end workflow for Boltz2 in BioIR. Use model_source="boltz-2". Protein chains require an MSA; paired or unpaired MSAs are accepted for inputs with multiple non-identical protein chains. You can optionally supply templates yourself because BioIR does not run HHsearch or HMMsearch. The end-to-end processor supports ligand structure prediction, but not ligand-affinity prediction.

Replace the truncated sequence and MSA path with valid values. For Ray tests, build rows from a real worklist with more records than replicas; do not repeat one row as evidence of useful scaling.

BioIR has two executor backends for the end-to-end processor workflow: serial and Ray. The serial backend runs each stage in sequence for one input, completing the full workflow before moving to the next input. This makes it useful for checking your setup before using the Ray backend to process independent inputs concurrently in Step 3.

model_inference_time is BioIR’s CUDA-synchronized folding-model forward measurement. It excludes parsing, tokenization, feature generation, postprocessing, and writing. Set the seed through the feature generator’s init_context. The scores field must be decoded, because it is a JSON string.

The Ray backend can be selected as follows, for the default replica layout:

This configuration places one complete model replica on each visible GPU on the current node, and sizes CPU stages from torch.cuda.device_count(). Below is an alternative configuration that controls four GPUs explicitly:

The capacity rule is engine_stage.compute × engine_stage.num_gpus ≤ visible GPUs. This four-replica example is a single-node configuration that assumes four visible GPUs. This tutorial does not cover multi-node deployment. Here Ray creates four engine actors and reserves one GPU for each. Every actor loads the full model. build_processor initializes Ray if needed. Actual throughput depends on input distribution, stage balance, storage, scheduling, and failures, so measure it.

In the ray end-to-end processor, the five processor stages consume inputs in this dependency order: Parser → Tokenizer → Feature generator → Folding engine → Writer. Configure each stage with its matching *StageConfig; the Step 3 example shows the relevant fields. The enabled field is not a public skip control. Each stage exposes compute; relevant stages also expose num_cpus, memory, and batch_size. The Ray engine adds max_concurrent_batches, accelerator_type, and num_gpus.

To tune the Ray pipeline, start with EngineProcessorConfig.create_default_replica_mode_config(...). Increase a stage’s compute to add workers; use num_cpus, memory, and, for engine actors, num_gpus to set resource reservations. Add parser, tokenizer, or feature workers if engines wait for inputs. Reduce concurrency or separate large inputs when GPU or object-store memory causes failures.

Ray is designed to overlap CPU stages with inference, but whether this improves the target workload depends on the run time cost of the parsing, feature generation, and output writing stages for a given input on a given hardware configuration. Refer to Figure 4 at ScaleFold to see the diversity in pre-processing times for OpenFold.

BioIR provides optimization at three distinct layers:

These layers target different bottlenecks. Kernel and module optimizations reduce model-forward time within a replica. Ray can increase worklist throughput by overlapping CPU stages with GPU folding and by running full-model replicas on separate GPUs for independent inputs. Ray does not split a single model forward pass across GPUs. Figure 1, above, distinguishes the processor and direct-integration paths; Ray scaling applies only to the processor path.

Our early benchmarking with BioNeMo Inference Runtime estimated the following model-forward accelerations:

Speedups measured using 1 warmup run (discarded) and 1 measurement call across 17 inputs spanning 29–1,734 residues. OpenFold3 and Boltz2 OSS baselines used torch.compile with dynamic=None, fullgraph=False, recompile_limit=128, accumulated_recompile_limit=256, fail_on_recompile_limit_hit=True. Boltz2 OSS used cuEq; OpenFold3 OSS used use_cuequivariance=True and use_deepspeed=True.

These results quantify acceleration within one model replica. They do not measure parsing, feature generation, output writing, Ray scheduling, multi-GPU throughput, or complete-worklist wall time. Figure 3, below, shows why model-forward and end-to-end measurements must remain separate.

To determine what additional GPUs unlock for a real deployment, measure the same representative worklist with one, two, and four Ray replicas on a single node. Step 6 defines the required metrics and comparison method.

To make these measurements concrete, we ran a matched benchmark on 1,000 human dimer targets with combined sequence lengths below 2,800 residues, representing a large collection of independent biomolecular structure-prediction tasks similar to the recently added dataset in the AlphaFold Database.

This representative folding-stage benchmark compares BioIR-accelerated Boltz-2 with a torch compiled open-source Boltz-2 implementation, on 8xH100 GPUs. Both implementations used the same targets, staged MSAs, inference recipe, and GPU configuration; throughput metrics and other results are specific to this configuration and should not be generalized to all BioIR-supported models, datasets, or hardware.

The workflow used three recycles, 200 sampling steps, and five diffusion samples per target. BioIR completed all 1,000 targets and delivered 58.5K successfully folded residues per allocated GPU-hour, compared with 20.2K for the public implementation—a 2.90× improvement in residue-normalized throughput; the open-source implementation ran out of memory on 29 targets.

The left panel of Figure 3, above, compares the model-forward times of the BioIR and torch-compiled open-source implementations and directly shows the lower model-forward time delivered by BioIR. The right panel of Figure 3 compares the throughput delivered by BioIR with the open-source implementation, where throughput is the total number of residues in the predicted structures normalized by allocated GPU-hours. The right panel of Figure 3 shows the speedup delivered by the kernel-level, module-level, and pipeline-level optimizations in BioIR. The left panel of Figure 3 shows the speedup delivered by the kernel-level and module-level implementations.

Similar to Boltz2 accelerations, BIR also enables faster inference for other biomolecular cofolding models, such as OpenFold2 and OpenFold3. An early version of BIR contributed accelerated modules to an NVIDIA-internal version of OpenFold2-MM, which enabled protein structure predictions at scale for the AFDB with 31 million protein complex structures.

We linearly extrapolated the 1000-target matched benchmark from Figure 3 to one million comparable targets using rated-power equivalents for an 8 x H100 80GB HBM3 node (see Figure 4, below).

BioIR is estimated to require 11 MWh versus 35 MWh for the public implementation using 8-GPU TDP (Thermal Design Power) equivalents, and 21 MWh versus 64 MWh using full-node maximum-power equivalents. These are folding-only estimates for IT equipment, not metered energy measurements, and exclude data center overhead, such as power usage effectiveness (PUE).

The controlled comparison measures folding throughput with the same inputs and MSAs for each implementation; it excludes MSA generation, preprocessing CPU allocations, storage, data transfer, retries, and engineering overhead. Report end-to-end pipeline performance metrics as distinct from model-forward metrics, including completed structures per hour, GPU and CPU utilization, peak GPU memory, completion rate, failures, and retries.

Explore BioNeMo Inference Runtime (BioIR) and integrate it into your structure prediction workflows at scale: http://github.com/NVIDIA-BioNeMo/BioNeMo-Inference-Runtime

To further accelerate drug discovery workflows with agentic orchestration, check out NVIDIA BioNeMo Agent Toolkit (BAT).

For the latest acceleration numbers, consult the API reference and support matrix.

生物分子结构预测目前通常在蛋白质组尺度上运行，其目标是高效地推进整个工作清单通过流水线。

NVIDIA BioNeMo 推理运行时（BioIR）有助于在 NVIDIA GPU 上加速所支持的生物分子结构预测模型，同时保留开发者熟悉的 PyTorch 工作流。它采用优化算子，并在适用情况下利用 CUDA Graphs 来加速模型执行。对于大批量的独立输入，Ray 可以在单节点的每个 GPU 上运行一个完整的模型副本，以提升整体吞吐量。

BioIR 还已被应用于真实的蛋白质组尺度工作中，包括近期 AlphaFold 数据库（AFDB）的扩展，加速了跨 4,777 个蛋白质组的蛋白质复合物结构生成——候选复合物总计约 3,100 万个，其中 181 万个作为高置信度预测结果发布。

你可以通过两种方式使用它（见下方图 1）：

本教程将逐步介绍 BioIR 的端到端处理器，涵盖从输入准备到 GPU 推理以及 PDB 或 mmCIF 格式输出的全流程，并展示如何追踪每小时预测结构数以及资源使用效率。

该 wheel 安装包包含预编译的 CUBIN 文件，因此运行时无需 nvcc、CUDA 源码、CMake 或 CUDA 工具包。

在下文中，我们将演示 BioIR 中 Boltz2 的端到端工作流。请使用 model_source="boltz-2"。蛋白质链需要多序列比对（MSA）；对于包含多个非同一蛋白质链的输入，支持成对或非成对 MSA。你可以选择自行提供模板，因为 BioIR 不会运行 HHsearch 或 HMMsearch。端到端处理器支持配体结构预测，但不支持配体亲和力预测。

请将截断的序列和 MSA 路径替换为有效值。对于 Ray 测试，请从记录数多于副本数的真实工作清单中构建行数据；不要通过重复单行数据来作为有用扩展能力的验证依据。

BioIR 为端到端处理器工作流提供了两种执行器后端：串行（serial）和 Ray。串行后端针对单个输入按顺序运行每个阶段，在转入下一个输入之前完成整个工作流。这使得它非常适合在步骤 3 中使用 Ray 后端并发处理独立输入之前，用于检查你的配置环境。

model_inference_time 是 BioIR 经过 CUDA 同步的折叠模型前向计算耗时度量。它不包括解析、分词、特征生成、后处理和写出阶段。可通过特征生成器的 init_context 设置随机种子。scores 字段必须进行解码，因为它是 JSON 字符串。

可以通过如下方式选择 Ray 后端以使用默认副本布局：

该配置会在当前节点上的每个可见 GPU 上放置一个完整的模型副本，并根据 torch.cuda.device_count() 来配置 CPU 阶段的资源规模。以下是显式控制四个 GPU 的另一种替代配置：

容量规则为 engine_stage.compute × engine_stage.num_gpus ≤ 可见 GPU 数量。这个四副本示例是假定具备四个可见 GPU 的单节点配置。本教程不涉及多节点部署。在此配置下，Ray 会创建四个引擎 actor 并为每个 actor 预留一个 GPU。每个 actor 都会加载完整模型。如果需要，build_processor 会初始化 Ray。实际吞吐量取决于输入分布、阶段均衡度、存储、调度以及故障情况，因此请进行实际测量。

在 Ray 端到端处理器中，五个处理阶段按照以下依赖顺序消费输入：解析器（Parser）→ 分词器（Tokenizer）→ 特征生成器（Feature generator）→ 折叠引擎（Folding engine）→ 写入器（Writer）。使用对应的 *StageConfig 配置每个阶段；步骤 3 的示例展示了相关字段。enabled 字段并非公开的跳过控制开关。每个阶段都会公开 compute；相关阶段还会公开 num_cpus、memory 和 batch_size。Ray 引擎则补充了 max_concurrent_batches、accelerator_type 和 num_gpus。

要调优 Ray 流水线，建议从 EngineProcessorConfig.create_default_replica_mode_config(...) 开始。增加某个阶段的 compute 可以添加 worker；使用 num_cpus、memory 以及针对引擎 actor 的 num_gpus 来设置资源预留。如果引擎在等待输入，请增加解析器、分词器或特征生成 worker。当 GPU 或对象存储内存导致运行故障时，请降低并发度或拆分大尺寸输入。

Ray 旨在将 CPU 阶段与推理重叠进行，但这种方式是否能改善目标工作负载，取决于在特定硬件配置下给定输入的解析、特征生成和输出写入阶段的运行耗时。有关 OpenFold 预处理时间的多样性，请参阅 ScaleFold 的图 4。

BioIR 在三个不同层级提供优化：

这些层级针对不同的性能瓶颈。算子和模块级优化可减少单副本内的模型前向传播时间。Ray 可以通过将 CPU 阶段与 GPU 折叠计算重叠，并在独立的 GPU 上为独立输入运行全模型副本，从而提高工作清单的吞吐量。Ray 不会将单个模型的前向传递拆分到多个 GPU 上。上方的图 1 区分了处理器路径和直接集成路径；Ray 扩展仅适用于处理器路径。

我们在 BioNeMo 推理运行时上的早期基准测试评估了以下模型前向加速效果：

加速比通过 1 次预热运行（弃用）和 1 次测量调用测得，测试覆盖了包含 29 至 1,734 个残基的 17 个输入。OpenFold3 和 Boltz2 开源基线采用 torch.compile，配置参数为 dynamic=None、fullgraph=False、recompile_limit=128、accumulated_recompile_limit=256、fail_on_recompile_limit_hit=True。Boltz2 开源版本使用了 cuEq；OpenFold3 开源版本使用了 use_cuequivariance=True 和 use_deepspeed=True。

这些结果量化了单个模型副本内部的加速效果。它们并未衡量解析、特征生成、输出写入、Ray 调度、多 GPU 吞吐量或完整工作清单的挂钟时间。下方的图 3 展示了为何必须将模型前向测量与端到端测量分开。

要确定额外的 GPU 能为实际部署带来什么收益，请在单节点上使用一个、两个和四个 Ray 副本测量相同的代表性工作清单。步骤 6 定义了所需的指标和对比方法。

为了使这些测量更加具体，我们在 1,000 个合并序列长度低于 2,800 个残基的人类二聚体靶标上运行了匹配的基准测试，这些靶标代表了大量独立的生物分子结构预测任务，类似于近期添加到 AlphaFold 数据库中的数据集。

这一具有代表性的折叠阶段基准测试在 8xH100 GPU 上对比了经过 BioIR 加速的 Boltz-2 与经过 torch.compile 的开源 Boltz-2 实现。两种实现使用了相同的靶标、预置 MSA、推理配置和 GPU 配置；吞吐量指标及其他结果专属于该配置，不应推广至所有 BioIR 支持的模型、数据集或硬件环境。

该工作流程使用了 3 次循环（recycles）、200 个采样步数，以及每个目标 5 个扩散样本。BioIR 完成了所有 1,000 个目标，并在每个分配的 GPU 小时内交付了 5.85 万个成功折叠的残基，而公开实现方案仅为 2.02 万个——残基归一化吞吐量提升了 2.90 倍；开源实现方案在 29 个目标上出现了内存不足（OOM）。

上文图 3 的左侧面板对比了 BioIR 与经过 torch 编译的开源实现方案的模型前向传播时间，直接展示了 BioIR 所实现的更低模型前向传播时间。图 3 的右侧面板对比了 BioIR 与开源实现方案所提供的吞吐量，其中吞吐量是指预测结构中的残基总数按分配的 GPU 小时数进行归一化后的结果。图 3 右侧面板展示了 BioIR 中算子级、模块级和流水线级优化所带来的加速。图 3 左侧面板则展示了算子级和模块级实现所带来的加速。

与 Boltz2 的加速类似，BIR 还为其他生物分子协同折叠模型（例如 OpenFold2 和 OpenFold3）提供了更快的推理能力。BIR 的早期版本为 NVIDIA 内部版本的 OpenFold2-MM 贡献了加速模块，从而支持了 AlphaFold 数据库（AFDB）的大规模蛋白质结构预测，涵盖 3100 万个蛋白质复合物结构。

我们根据 8 张 H100 80GB HBM3 节点的额定功率等效值，将图 3 中 1000 个目标的匹配基准线性外推至 100 万个可比目标（见下方图 4）。

据估计，在采用 8-GPU TDP（热设计功耗）等效值计算时，BioIR 需要 11 MWh，而公开实现方案需要 35 MWh；在采用整节点最大功率等效值计算时，BioIR 需要 21 MWh，而公开实现方案需要 64 MWh。这些仅是针对 IT 设备的折叠估算，并非实际测量的能耗数值，并且不包括数据中心开销（例如电能使用效率 PUE）。

该对照比较是在每个实现方案使用相同输入和多序列比对（MSA）的情况下测量折叠吞吐量；它排除了 MSA 生成、预处理 CPU 分配、存储、数据传输、重试以及工程开销。报告将端到端流水线性能指标与模型前向传播指标区分开来，包括每小时完成的结构数、GPU 和 CPU 利用率、峰值 GPU 显存占用、完成率、失败次数以及重试次数。

aiStories.title: AI智能体正以海量新请求淹没公共服务机构
aiStories.originalTitle: AI agents are flooding public services with new requests
aiStories.snippet: “The vast majority of cases we find are people who are entitled to claim for something, claiming for that thing,” the researcher told TechCrunch.
aiStories.fullContent:
As AI makes it easier to fill forms and file complaints, public services around the world are seeing enormous jumps in applications and other requests.

In the United Kingdom, complaints to the housing ombudsman more than doubled since the introduction of ChatGPT, rising from 2600 in 2022 to just over 7,000 last year. The United States’ Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) saw 5x growth in complaints over the same period. There were similar jumps in Brazilian judicial petitions and German parliamentary petitions.

Researcher Chris Schmitz is tracking this rise as part of a broader trend he called “agentic flooding.” In a paper set to be presented next month at the AI Ethics and Society conference, he looks at 84 different cases of potential flooding across 11 jurisdictions, finding broad evidence that AI tools are changing the way people interact with public services.

The harder question is what to do in response. While some of the new filings are clearly adversarial, others are the result of legitimate applicants using AI to file claims that would otherwise be abandoned. While some might see the new applications as AI-generated spam, Schmitz sees it as a rare opportunity to remake social services for the AI era.

Schmitz looked at services ranging from welfare applications to official judicial appeals, but they all have online services that could be accessed by an AI assistant. (The full dataset is hosted here, for reference). For methodological reasons, Schmitz’s paper stops short of saying AI is directly causing the surge of new applicants. But most of the 84 cases follow the same basic arc, where submissions were roughly flat before 2022, then rose at increasing speed as AI technology diffuses. Crucially, most cases have not seen that growth slow down, suggesting it will likely keep rising for years to come.

For Schmitz, it’s easy to see how the increasing skills and availability of AI would drive increased usage.

“People are finding out that this is something one can do, and incrementally, it is just getting easier to do it…before it might have been a question of a lot of dragging context together and prompting ChatGPT 3.5 very precisely, it may now be a question of just pasting or taking a photo of a letter with your Claude app and getting a pretty good response in one shot,” he said.

The jump in volume is similar to what many bug-bounty services also experienced last year, as companies found their inboxes flooded with low-quality reports generated by LLMs. The reports rarely contained significant security issues, but companies were still obligated to vet the reports as they came in, presenting a significant drain on resources. It’s easy to imagine public services facing a similar problem, as they manage five times more applicants with the same budget.

But where the bug bounty programs were flooded with worthless submissions, Schmitz says most of the new applications to public services are coming from real people with legitimate claims.

“The vast majority of cases we find are people who are entitled to claim for something, claiming for that thing,” he told TechCrunch.

If those people weren’t claiming the benefits before, it may have been because the work of applying was too forbidding — something known in the policy world as administrative burden. Now that AI can lift that burden, it could be an opportunity to remake many of these services in a more AI-friendly way.

It’s a major task, which we mostly haven’t begun to tackle, but Schmitz sees it as reason for optimism.

“A big part of making AI go well is being able to detail out what the good version of things looks like. And anyone who’s ever used ChatGPT to do the tax return knows that there’s a good version here where you’re being helped,” Schmitz says. “This could be the moment to say, ‘we need to rethink pretty much everything about how this process looks.’”

aiStories.fullTranslation:
随着人工智能（AI）让填写表格和提交投诉变得更加容易，世界各地的公共服务机构正面临着申请和其他请求的大幅激增。

在英国，自ChatGPT推出以来，向住房申诉专员（housing ombudsman）提交的投诉量增加了一倍以上，从2022年的2600起增加到去年的7000多起。同期，美国消费者金融保护局（CFPB）收到的投诉量激增了5倍。巴西的司法诉求和德国的议会请愿中也出现了类似的剧烈增长。

研究员克里斯·施密茨（Chris Schmitz）正在追踪这一激增趋势，并将其视作他称之为“智能体洪泛”（agentic flooding）的更广泛趋势的一部分。在定于下个月举行的AI伦理与社会大会（AI Ethics and Society conference）上发表的一篇论文中，他考察了11个司法管辖区内84起潜在的洪泛案例，发现了AI工具正在改变人们与公共服务交互方式的大量证据。

更难的问题在于该如何应对。尽管一些新提交的文件显然带有对抗性，但另一些则是合法申请者利用AI提交了原本可能会被放弃的索赔或诉求。尽管有些人可能会将这些新申请视作AI生成的垃圾信息，但施密茨将其视为一个难得的契机，可以借此为AI时代重塑社会服务体系。

施密茨考察的服务涵盖了从福利申请到正式司法上诉等领域，但它们都拥有可被AI助手访问的在线服务（完整数据集托管于此处以供参考）。出于方法论原因，施密茨的论文并未直接断言AI直接导致了新申请者的激增。但在这84个案例中，绝大多数都遵循着相同的基本轨迹：在2022年之前，提交量大致保持平稳，随后随着AI技术的普及以越来越快的速度攀升。至关重要的是，大多数案例并未出现增长放缓的迹象，这表明在未来几年里增长很可能会继续保持。

在施密茨看来，AI技能的增强和易用性的提升将推动使用率的增加，这一点显而易见。

“人们发现这是可以做到的事情，而且逐渐地，操作变得越来越容易……以前可能需要把很多上下文信息拖到一起，并非常精准地向ChatGPT 3.5输入提示词，而现在可能只需要把信件粘贴到Claude应用程序中或直接拍张照片，就能一次性得到相当不错的回应，”他表示。

业务量的激增与去年许多漏洞赏金服务所经历的情况相似，当时企业发现自己的收件箱被大语言模型（LLM）生成的低质量报告所淹没。这些报告极少包含重大的安全漏洞，但企业仍有义务在收到报告时进行审核，从而造成了巨大的资源消耗。不难想象，在预算相同的情况下要处理5倍于以往的申请人，公共服务机构也正面临着类似的问题。

然而，与漏洞赏金项目中充斥着毫无价值的提交内容不同，施密茨表示，向公共服务机构提交的大多数新申请都来自拥有合法诉求的真实个人。

“在我们发现的绝大多数案例中，都是有资格申请某项权益的人在申领该权益，”他向TechCrunch表示。

如果这些人以前没有申领这些福利，可能是因为申请流程过于繁琐复杂——这在政策界被称为行政负担（administrative burden）。现在既然AI可以减轻这种负担，这或许是一个以更契合AI的方式重塑诸多此类服务的契机。

这是一项艰巨的任务，我们基本上尚未开始着手应对，但施密茨对此持乐观态度。

“让AI发挥良好作用的一个重要部分，在于能够明确阐述事物向好发展时的样貌。任何曾使用ChatGPT报税的人都知道，在这类场景中存在着一种你真正得到帮助的良好状态，”施密茨说。“这或许正是一个契机，让我们意识到：‘我们需要从根本上重新反思这一流程的一切呈现方式。’”

aiStories.fullContent:

See All Entertainment

Jimmy Kimmel is the latest talk show host to move an interview with Talarico online after the FCC ‘threatened’ him.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

See All by Stevie Bonifield

Jimmy Kimmel will be interviewing Democratic Texas Senate candidate James Talarico “under unusual circumstances,” posting the interview directly to YouTube, rather than airing it on TV during Jimmy Kimmel Live. In Wednesday night’s episode, Kimmel said this was out of concern for retaliation from the Trump administration’s FCC:

[Trump’s] FCC has threatened me, threatened our show, threatened our network, ABC, our affiliates, our local stations based on simple, traditional editorial decisions, guest bookings, it would seem they don’t like. And so, out of consideration for our local stations, especially our ABC affiliates in Texas who would have to deal with this nonsense, my interview tomorrow with James Talarico will not air on television. It will be posted on YouTube instead. It will not be on TV.

Kimmel’s announcement comes almost a year after his show was taken off the air in response to threats from FCC chair Brendan Carr. In February, Stephen Colbert also had to move an interview with Talarico to YouTube, claiming CBS barred him from airing it over worries about upsetting the FCC, citing the FCC’s equal time rule. The FCC also took aim at The View after an interview with Talarico earlier this year.

ABC, which airs Jimmy Kimmel Live and The View, filed a lawsuit against the FCC last month claiming it has “waged a retaliatory campaign” against its networks, “punishing” ABC by threatening to pull its broadcast licenses.

aiStories.title: Bending Spoons将以13.6亿美元收购协作工具开发商Miro，较2022年估值缩水逾90%
aiStories.originalTitle: Bending Spoons to buy collaboration tools maker Miro for $1.36B, 90% less than its 2022 valuation
aiStories.snippet: Bending Spoons is buying Miro for $1.36B, a huge dip in valuation for the workplace collaboration startup, which was valued at $17.5B in late 2021.
aiStories.fullContent:
Bending Spoons is continuing its trend of buying once-sought-after software companies for pennies on the dollar. This time, the Italian company is buying Miro for $1.36 billion in cash (equity value of $1.79 billion), a mighty dip in valuation for the once-hot workplace collaboration startup that was awarded a price tag of $17.5 billion in late 2021.

Founded in 2011 as a whiteboarding tool called RealtimeBoard, Miro found great fortune during the COVID-19 pandemic, when companies moved to remote work en masse, and found their employees wanting to replicate the experience of collaborating on a physical whiteboard.

Miro quickly capitalized on that momentum by building a platform that could integrate with more than 250 apps, and struck partnerships with Atlassian, Cisco, Microsoft, and Zoom. The company also started letting its users build integrations with common tools and customize the base product to meet their needs. Today, it calls itself an “AI innovation workspace” that offers AI assistants for its whiteboard tools, AI workflows, prototyping tools, and AI connectors that pull context from various platforms like GitHub, Jira, and Slack.

By 2022, Miro had grown from five million to about 30 million users within a scant two years, and its paying customer base had expanded by 550% — factors that likely contributed to its immense valuation at the time.

By all indications, the company has continued growing, though not at that blistering pace. Today, Miro has more than four million paying users and 100 million total users. Bending Spoons said Miro now has about $600 million in annual recurring revenue, of which 90% comes from businesses and enterprises. The company also has about $435 million in net cash, and is profitable.

Still, the 92% dip in Miro’s valuation is illustrative of just how much software-as-a-service (SaaS) multiples have unwound since its heydays of 2021. By 2022, the dying pandemic tailwinds spurred companies to tighten spending by cutting down on duplicate apps and licenses. Miro, competing with much-better funded rivals such as Canva, Figma, and Microsoft in the workplace collaboration space, likely found itself shoved aside as businesses started preferring suites of various products instead of individual collaboration tools.

Miro, which had about 1,200 employees in 2022, cut jobs twice, laying off 119 staff in February 2023 and reportedly another 275 people in October 2024.

Bending Spoons, however, is probably happy it is able to snap up a company that’s been doing quite well for a smidgen of its former, arguably inflated, value. In that way, Miro is pretty similar to Airtable, which was valued at over $11 billion in the boom days of 2021, but sold to Bending Spoons for $1.28 billion last month.

The Italian serial acquirer of software companies seems to be exploiting a specific change: Large, recognizable SaaS companies that were priced in 2021 as if they’d become software giants, but matured into slower-growing but still substantial businesses with decent recurring revenue and established user bases.

Still, it’s curious why Miro’s board and investors agreed to sell at that price now, especially seeing that the company didn’t apparently need the cash. Has confidence in SaaS companies being able to go public or find a comparable exit really plummeted that low?

Bending Spoons 正在延续其以极其低廉的价格收购昔日热门软件公司的势头。这一次，这家意大利公司将以 13.6 亿美元现金（股权价值为 17.9 亿美元）收购 Miro。对于这家曾在 2021 年底获得 17.5 亿美元估值的热门办公协作初创企业而言，估值出现了大幅下滑。

Miro 成立于 2011 年，最初是一款名为 RealtimeBoard 的在线白板工具。在新冠疫情期间，由于各大企业纷纷转向远程办公，且员工希望重现实体白板协作的体验，Miro 迎来了爆发式增长。

Miro 迅速抓住这一机遇，构建了一个可与超过 250 款应用程序集成的平台，并与 Atlassian、思科（Cisco）、微软（Microsoft）以及 Zoom 建立了合作关系。该公司还开始允许用户自行构建与常用工具的集成，并定制基础产品以满足自身需求。如今，它自称为“AI 创新工作空间”，为其白板工具提供 AI 助手、AI 工作流、原型设计工具，以及能从 GitHub、Jira 和 Slack 等各类平台提取上下文信息的 AI 连接器。

截至 2022 年，Miro 在短短两年内用户数就从 500 万激增至约 3000 万，其付费客户群增长了 550%——这些因素很可能是促成其当时超高估值的原因。

从各方面迹象来看，该公司仍在继续增长，尽管速度已不复当年的迅猛。如今，Miro 拥有超过 400 万付费用户和 1 亿总用户。Bending Spoons 表示，Miro 目前的年度经常性收入（ARR）约为 6 亿美元，其中 90% 来自企业和商业客户。此外，该公司还拥有约 4.35 亿美元的净现金，且处于盈利状态。

尽管如此，Miro 估值缩水 92% 的事实，仍充分表明了软件即服务（SaaS）的估值倍数自 2021 年巅峰时期以来经历了多么剧烈的回落。到了 2022 年，逐渐消退的疫情红利促使企业通过精简重复的应用和软件许可来缩减开支。在办公协作领域，面对 Canva、Figma 和微软等资金更为充裕的对手，随着企业开始更青睐综合产品套件而非单一协作工具，Miro 很可能发现自己逐渐被边缘化。

Miro 在 2022 年拥有约 1200 名员工，此后经历过两次裁员：先是在 2023 年 2 月裁撤了 119 名员工，据报道又在 2024 年 10 月裁掉了 275 人。

然而，Bending Spoons 或许很高兴能够以仅占过去（甚至被认为是虚高的）估值极小一部分的价格，拿下这样一家表现尚属稳健的公司。就这一点而言，Miro 与 Airtable 极为相似——后者在 2021 年繁荣时期的估值超过 110 亿美元，但上个月以 12.8 亿美元被 Bending Spoons 收购。

这家来自意大利的软件连续收购方似乎正在把握一种特定的转变：那些在 2021 年被赋予软件巨头般估值、极具知名度的大型 SaaS 公司，如今已演变为增长放缓但规模依然可观的企业，拥有扎实的经常性收入和成熟的用户群。

然而令人费解的是，Miro 的董事会和投资者为何同意在此时以这个价格出售，特别是考虑到该公司表面上并不缺钱。人们对 SaaS 公司成功上市或实现类似退出的信心，难道真的已经跌到如此谷底了吗？

aiStories.title: Maven Robotics 意欲抢下你的机器人部署订单
aiStories.originalTitle: Maven Robotics wants to steal your robot deployment deal
aiStories.snippet: Maven Robotics emerged from stealth today with a $100 million Series A and active deployments.
aiStories.fullContent:
In 2024, Maven Robotics was brand new, and they had nothing—”a cartoon of a robot and a team of people,” CEO and co-founder Hamza Derbas told TechCrunch.

Still, they heard a large consumer goods company with logistics needs was in town to meet with four rival robot companies about automation. Derbas talked his way into a meeting with the company and, instead of talking about his views on robots, asked to visit their factories and warehouses.

“We saw how people were working; we zeroed in on flows we could immediately bring value to,” he told TechCrunch. “We showed them that our approach to robotics is different—we’re not trying to solve a single robot problem. We’re trying to autonomously take on the task end to end: It hooks in from one side to a warehouse management system; product goes on trucks on the other side.”

They won the deal, beating out companies with existing robots. After two years of work with that company and a few other partners, Derbas says Maven has as many as eight robots working 16 hours a day, with 99% or higher uptime.

Today, the startup is emerging from stealth after raising $100 million from RoboStrategy, LocalGlobe, Vine Ventures, and XTX Markets Ventures, with plans to build 250 of their third-generation robots and begin design on a fourth-generation platform.

Their robots sit on wheeled bases, capable of moving 10 miles an hour, with two arms that can lift up to 30 kilograms. Their main job is “mixed palletizing”—wooden pallets carrying boxed goods come from different factories to a distribution center, where the robot creates a new pallet containing a mix of goods to be sent to a store.

“Within 48 hours of them putting the stuff on the shelves, they want to change the mix based on real-time demand. Here’s an order with different mixed [products] going to that retail store; please build it out. It’s all done with human labor today, running around the warehouse picking one of this, one of that.”

At Maven’s Santa Clara facility, the robot moves smoothly about its work in a training area, using vacuum suckers to pick up and arrange the boxes at a reasonable speed. A live video screen shows two robots working in a customer facility while employees walk around them.

Derbas spent his career in automotive engineering, with a focus on EVs, but before Maven he spent nine years working at Apple on the company’s special project group, which he wouldn’t discuss but is widely thought to have been building a self-driving car before it was disbanded in 2024. That was when he started Maven with his brother, Khalid, who serves as the company’s CFO after a career in private equity.

Like other physical AI companies, the firm relies on veterans of self-driving car efforts, which have developed the most sophisticated approaches to training autonomous hardware from real data. That requires data pipelines that return information from operating robots within minutes or hours—”then retrain, evaluate, run ablation studies, figure out what’s the right set of weights, redeploy, and then turn that loop again.”

In a crowded world of robot companies, Maven sets itself apart with its focus on the realities of industrial operation. Jack Pearson, an investor at RoboStrategy who backed the company, says what sets the company apart is its background in industrial systems, rather than a research culture that is optimized for learning or focused on a specific architecture.

Agility, the robotics company going public this fall in a $2.5 billion SPAC deal, might be the most similarly positioned firm in the market, focused on safety and specific industrial workflows. But its robots stand on two legs, something Derbas, while stressing his respect for the company, says “make zero sense for anything they’re doing…they are very complex, unreliable, and add unnecessary cost. ROI is the name of the game here.”

That understanding of the realities of overheated facilities and the needs of the people who operate them has helped them get the startup out the door, but if Maven wants to expand beyond its current workflows, it will figure out some kind of research culture. While palletization might be an $80 billion market, the next set of tasks the company is targeting will require robotic manipulation capabilities that don’t yet exist.

Maven’s next big push is to collect more data and train its robots to be able to handle materials, and then to move towards automation and fabrication. The company will draw on its own systems, tap third-party providers, and has even developed a pair of pincer-like gloves that allow humans to emulate the form factor they want for their grippers. While the company bills itself as a maker of general-purpose robots, its strategy is to go task-by-task towards that goal.“We’re grounded in solving one customer problem at a time,” Derbas said. “If you focus on solving problems and you pick sizeable problems, each problem is a multi-billion-dollar market. If you do that, there’s plenty of data to master these skills.”

That process might be the most viable path to putting robots in the workplace—or an opportunity to get one-shotted by the next powerful physical AI model to roll out of the frontier labs.

“We’re not in the race for models—we’re in the race to solve industrial labor and make this work possible at the scale the world needs,” Derbas told TechCrunch.

aiStories.fullTranslation:
2024 年时，Maven Robotics 还是一家初出茅庐的新公司，他们一无所有——只有“一张机器人草图和一个团队”，首席执行官兼联合创始人 Hamza Derbas 向 TechCrunch 表示。

尽管如此，他们听说一家有物流需求的大型消费品公司来到当地，准备就自动化事宜与四家竞争对手机器人公司会面。Derbas 想方设法争取到了与该公司会面的机会，但他没有空谈自己对机器人的看法，而是提出参观他们的工厂和仓库。

“我们看到了工人们是如何工作的；我们迅速锁定了那些能立即带来价值的流程，”他向 TechCrunch 说道。“我们向他们展示了我们在机器人技术上的与众不同——我们不是试图解决单一的机器人问题，而是试图端到端自主接管整项任务：它一端连接仓库管理系统，另一端把产品送上卡车。”

他们赢得了这笔订单，击败了那些已经拥有实体机器人的公司。在与该公司以及其他几个合作伙伴合作两年后，Derbas 表示 Maven 已有多达八台机器人每天工作 16 个小时，正常运行时间达到 99% 或更高。

如今，这家初创公司在从 RoboStrategy、LocalGlobe、Vine Ventures 和 XTX Markets Ventures 筹集到 1 亿美元后正式走出隐身状态，并计划制造 250 台第三代机器人，同时启动第四代平台的设计工作。

他们的机器人安装在轮式底盘上，移动速度可达每小时 10 英里，配备两只可举起多达 30 公斤重量的机械臂。它们的主要工作是“混合码垛”——装有箱装货物的木制托盘从不同工厂运送到配送中心，机器人在那里创建一个包含多种混合货物的新托盘，以便运往零售店。

“在把货物摆上货架的 48 小时内，他们希望根据实时需求改变组合搭配。比如这里有一份送往那家零售店的不同混合[产品]订单；请把它堆垛好。如今这完全依靠人力完成，工人们在仓库里到处跑，挑拣一件这个、一件那个。”

在 Maven 位于圣克拉拉的设施内，机器人在训练区平稳地开展工作，利用真空吸盘以适中的速度抓取和摆放箱子。现场视频屏幕显示两台机器人在客户的设施中工作，而员工们就在它们周围走动。

Derbas 的职业生涯始于汽车工程，重点专注于电动汽车，但在创立 Maven 之前，他在苹果公司的特殊项目组（SPG）工作了九年。他拒绝讨论该项目，但外界普遍认为该团队在 2024 年解散前一直致力于研发自动驾驶汽车。正是在那时，他与曾在私募股权行业工作的弟弟 Khalid 一同创办了 Maven，后者担任公司首席财务官。

与其它具身智能（physical AI）公司一样，该公司依赖自动驾驶汽车领域的资深人士，因为他们开发出了利用真实数据训练自主硬件的最前沿方法。这需要构建能够在几分钟或几小时内传回运行中机器人信息的数据管道——“然后重新训练、评估、运行消融实验、找出合适的权重组合、重新部署，接着再次循环推进。”

在拥挤的机器人公司赛道中，Maven 凭借对工业运营现实的专注脱颖而出。支持该公司的 RoboStrategy 投资人 Jack Pearson 表示，这家公司的独特之处在于其深厚的工业系统背景，而不是针对学习优化或专注于特定架构的研究文化。

今年秋季通过 25 亿美元 SPAC 交易上市的机器人公司 Agility 或许是市场上定位最相似的公司，同样专注于安全和特定的工业工作流。但其机器人采用双足直立形态，对此 Derbas 在强调对该公司的尊重的同时表示，“对于他们正在做的任何事情而言都毫无意义……它们非常复杂、不可靠，并且增加了不必要的成本。投资回报率（ROI）才是这里的核心所在。”

对闷热车间环境现实及其操作人员需求的这种深刻理解，帮助这家初创公司迈出了坚实的第一步，但如果 Maven 想拓展至当前工作流之外，就必须建立起某种研究文化。尽管码垛可能是一个价值 800 亿美元的市场，但该公司瞄准的下一阶段任务将需要目前尚不存在的机器人操作能力。

Maven 的下一步大动作是收集更多数据并训练其机器人处理物料，进而迈向自动化和制造工序。该公司将依靠自身系统，接入第三方供应商，甚至还开发了一副夹钳状手套，以便人类能够模拟出他们希望机械爪所呈现的外形规格。尽管该公司自诩为通用机器人制造商，但其战略是逐步攻克任务以实现该目标。“我们立足于一次解决一个客户问题，”Derbas 说道。“如果你专注于解决问题，并且挑选规模可观的问题，那么每个问题都对应着一个数十亿美元的市场。如果能做到这一点，就有海量的数据来掌握这些技能。”

这一过程可能是将机器人引入工作场所的最可行路径——或者也可能是一次被前沿实验室推出的下一个强大具身智能模型一击淘汰的风险。

“我们不在模型竞赛的赛道上——我们在解决工业劳动力问题、并以世界所需规模实现这项工作的赛道上，”Derbas 向 TechCrunch 表示。

aiStories.title: 亚马逊在ChatGPT中试点广告服务
aiStories.originalTitle: Amazon pilots ad services in ChatGPT
aiStories.fullContent:
Conversational ads inventory will be available as a managed service via Amazon DSP, but OpenAI will handle placement through its own systems.

The OpenAI tie-up provides Amazon a bridge into one of the most popular AI programs — a channel that is increasingly intersecting with the world of advertising and informing more consumer decision-making. For OpenAI, the pact may open a floodgate of new entrants to its ads business at a critical moment. Amazon operates the third-largest digital advertising platform and neared $70 billion in ads revenue last year.

ChatGPT Ads will be bought via Amazon DSP and are offered as a managed service, meaning Amazon’s team will help set up and optimize campaigns. Inventory will be available on both a cost-per-click and cost-per-mille, or cost per thousand impressions, basis. The pilot is limited to the U.S. at launch.

OpenAI will control all ad delivery decisions through its own systems, an Amazon spokesperson said. The ads themselves will surface as text and image units beneath organic ChatGPT responses with clearly marked sponsored labels, aligning with how OpenAI has served ads to date. ChatGPT currently runs ads on its free model and cheaper Go subscription tier. In addition, Amazon is offering product feed ads that automatically generate assets based on product catalogues.

Advertisers value Amazon for its troves of shopping and streaming data that can be used to improve marketing precision. ChatGPT for its part has pitched its advertising as a way to realize more contextually rich and relevant campaigns. Those testing the ChatGPT Ads integration will receive some aggregated performance data related to impressions, clicks, cost per result, CPM and CPC metrics. The concept could be appealing to nonendemic advertisers, or advertisers that wouldn’t typically sell goods on Amazon.

“Travel planning is becoming increasingly personalized, and travelers expect experiences that feel relevant,” Katrin Koenig, president of Delta Vacations, said in a statement. "Through our collaboration with Amazon Ads and ChatGPT Ads, we can leverage deep consumer insights to inform how and when Delta Vacations appear within ChatGPT Ads experiences to create new opportunities for travelers to engage and discover vacation possibilities.”

OpenAI began testing ChatGPT ads in February and has quickly built out the business as it prepares for a highly anticipated initial public offering where the segment could play a role in the company’s revenue-generation narrative. The decision to run ads has drawn flak from competitors while industry reports indicate some marketers have been underwhelmed by performance. OpenAI previously partnered with other retail media networks, including those operated by Target and Albertsons, but Amazon’s is significantly larger.

ChatGPT ads late last month achieved a $1 billion in annualized revenue run rate, a projection of expected annual revenue based on shorter-term gains. OpenAI says tens of thousands of advertisers use the service, which recently expanded in India, Europe, the Middle East and North Africa. It has also enlisted third parties to refine its capabilites in areas that are important for building advertising confidence, including working with LiveRamp on measurement.

OpenAI linking with an established DSP in its quest for scale isn’t particularly surprising, but its initial pick of partner could be. The software developer reportedly discussed a deal with The Trade Desk, an independent rival of Amazon’s, earlier this year.
aiStories.fullTranslation:
对话式广告资源将作为托管服务通过 Amazon DSP（亚马逊需求方平台）提供，但 OpenAI 将通过其自身系统处理广告投放。

与 OpenAI 的联手为亚马逊搭建了一座通往最受欢迎的 AI 应用之一的桥梁——这一渠道正日益与广告领域深度融合，并对更多消费者的决策产生影响。对于 OpenAI 而言，该协议可能在一个关键时刻为其广告业务打开迎来海量新参与者的大门。亚马逊运营着全球第三大数字广告平台，去年的广告收入接近 700 亿美元。

ChatGPT 广告将通过 Amazon DSP 进行采购，并作为一项托管服务提供，这意味着亚马逊团队将协助建立并优化广告投放项目。广告资源将同时支持按每次点击费用（CPC）和千次展示费用（CPM）进行结算。该试点项目在推出初期仅限于美国地区。

亚马逊一位发言人表示，OpenAI 将通过其自身系统掌控所有广告投放决策。广告本身将以文本和图片单元的形式出现在 ChatGPT 自然生成的回答下方，并带有清晰标记的赞助商标识，这与 OpenAI 迄今为止投放广告的方式保持一致。ChatGPT 目前在其免费版本和价格较低的 Go 订阅层级中展示广告。此外，亚马逊还提供商品信息流广告（product feed ads），可基于商品目录自动生成广告物料素材。

广告商看重亚马逊海量的购物和流媒体数据，这些数据可用于提升营销精准度。ChatGPT 方面则将其广告定位为一种实现更具上下文丰富度及高相关性营销活动的方式。参与测试 ChatGPT 广告整合方案的客户将获得一些汇总效果数据，涵盖展示次数、点击量、单次转化费用、CPM 以及 CPC 等指标。这一概念可能对非固有广告商（即通常不在亚马逊平台上销售商品的广告主）具有吸引力。

达美假期（Delta Vacations）总裁卡特琳·柯尼格（Katrin Koenig）在一份声明中表示：“旅行规划正变得日益个性化，旅行者期望获得具有相关性的体验。通过与亚马逊广告及 ChatGPT 广告的合作，我们可以利用深度的消费者洞察，指导达美假期在 ChatGPT 广告体验中出现的时机与方式，为旅行者参与互动并探索各种度假可能创造新机会。”

OpenAI 于 2 月开始测试 ChatGPT 广告，并在筹备备受期待的首次公开募股（IPO）之际迅速拓展该业务，广告板块有望在公司的创收叙事中发挥重要作用。展示广告的决定招致了竞争对手的批评，而行业报告显示，一些营销人员对其效果反应平平。OpenAI 此前曾与其他零售媒体网络合作，包括塔吉特（Target）和艾伯森（Albertsons）运营的网络，但亚马逊的网络规模明显更为庞大。

上个月底，ChatGPT 广告的年化营收运转率（即根据短期收益推算的预期年收入）达到了 10 亿美元。OpenAI 表示，已有数以万计的广告商在使用这项服务，该服务近期已拓展至印度、欧洲、中东和北非地区。它还引入了第三方机构以完善对建立广告信心至关重要的各项能力，包括与 LiveRamp 合作开展成效衡量。

OpenAI 在追求规模扩张的过程中与成熟的 DSP 联手并不令人意外，但其最初挑选的合作伙伴或许耐人寻味。据报道，这家软件开发商今年早些时候曾与亚马逊的独立竞争对手 The Trade Desk 商讨过交易事宜。

aiStories.title: Shopify 放弃 React Native 回归原生开发
aiStories.originalTitle: Shopify moves back to Native from React Native
aiStories.fullContent:
Coding agents changed what it costs to build mobile apps twice. Here’s why Shopify is moving from React Native back to Swift and Kotlin.

Engineering at Shopify

We decided to go all-in on React Native back in 2020, and that bet has been extremely successful. We saved a ton of time building features just once, enabled developers with no mobile background to contribute to our apps, and freed ourselves from constantly chasing feature parity.

In January 2025, I wrote that the future of React Native was bright and that Shopify planned to keep investing in it. That was true based on what we knew then. React Native was working well for us, and it remains an excellent framework. But since then, coding models have gotten dramatically better, and for our apps and our team, building the same feature in Swift and Kotlin no longer carries the cost it used to.

We don’t hold on to a decision just because it was successful at the time. When a core assumption changes, we’re willing to go back and ask whether it’s still the right call. LLMs changed one of the core assumptions behind our 2020 decision, so we reevaluated our mobile stack from first principles.

What we found led us back to native.

We decided to switch from native to React Native in 2020 for three reasons:

React Native consistently delivered these benefits. We found ourselves spending a significant amount of time and resources on optimizing performance, improving key foundational areas in React Native, and keeping up with framework updates and external dependencies, but these were acceptable tradeoffs. The benefits of using React Native far outweighed the investments we had to make in these areas.

Shopify has been using LLMs to build software since 2021 (one year before ChatGPT!). Initially, we used them to implement features, investigate and fix bugs, and review code. As the models improved, so did the complexity of the work we trusted them to take on. By late 2025, they were no longer just helping us write code faster. They were capable of making us question whether building software twice still meant doing twice the work.

We decided to reevaluate our mobile tech stack and started prototyping to see whether our technology choices still held up. We rebuilt several core parts of our biggest apps in Swift and Kotlin using LLMs and were surprised by how well it worked. Agents:

Native still means building and maintaining software on two platforms, that cost has not disappeared. What changed is that agents can now do enough of the implementation, translation, testing, and review work that it’s no longer the deciding factor it was in 2020.

React Native apps can be fast. Ours are. We are making this change because agents have reduced the advantages of sharing implementation, while the advantages of building for each platform remain. Native keeps us closer to platform capabilities and first-party tooling, with fewer framework and dependency layers between our code and the platform.

Before we get into how we’re migrating, we want to make sure we do this transition cleanly. From the beginning, we wanted to contribute back to React Native to make it better. We’ve published open-source libraries that have become the top choice in their respective categories. We’re grateful for the incredible reception from the community and are committed to making sure this is a smooth transition with no surprises.

Shopify will continue sponsoring this through the end of 2026, and William Candillon will continue working on it beyond that. He will fork the repo in the coming months and start publishing the library under a new name. The original repo will be archived when this transition is complete. We’ll post updates along the way so that everyone has ample time to migrate. If your app relies on this library, please consider sponsoring it.

This library gets ~2M downloads/week and has become the default way to render high-performance lists in React Native. Given how important it is for the ecosystem, Shopify will continue to fix critical issues that break compatibility. We’re currently in discussions with several companies about taking on long-term stewardship of FlashList. If you’re interested, reach out to me here.

Restyle has a smaller user base than our other libraries, so we're archiving this repo. We'll keep it working through the end of 2026, then stop maintaining it. Anyone is welcome to fork it and take it forward, and we'll help with the handover if a team wants to pick it up.

Shopify has several large apps (Shopify, Shop, Point of Sale, Inbox). Millions of merchants and buyers around the world rely on them every single day to earn their livelihood and buy products they want from the brands they love.

We debated between gradually migrating to native (brownfield) versus rebuilding them from scratch (greenfield). In the past when we migrated to React Native, we picked the brownfield approach for some of our biggest apps, as it’d take years to rewrite them and we’d have to stop shipping new features while the rewrite was in progress.

However, this time greenfield emerged as a clear winner for the following reasons:

The Shop app, which is regularly at the top of the list in the shopping category in the app stores, is the first to be migrated. Assisted by AI, the team was able to go from a proof of concept to a fully rebuilt native app published in the app stores in just 12 weeks. We’ve written about this migration in depth here.

The migration of the Shopify app (our biggest with 300+ screens, home & lockscreen widgets, Apple Watch app, complications, Siri Shortcuts, etc.), is also underway and will ship later this year. The rest of our apps will be migrated soon.

It’s tempting to just point an LLM to the React Native codebase and try to one-shot the same features in native, but it doesn’t work. Even if you ask it to gather as much information as it can up front, freeze that into specs, task files, and then implement it, you end up with a huge amount of unmaintainable code that can’t be shipped.

To solve this problem, we built a system called Helix that takes a more gradual approach. It doesn't expect the first output to be correct, and builds a loop where an imperfect attempt simply cannot move forward until it becomes a good result.

The developer points Helix at a screen. Helix reads the React Native code and proposes a sequence of checkpoints (small, ordered slices of the work) that can be reviewed in minutes. Then, checkpoint by checkpoint, it builds: each one must prove its behavior with tests, match the running app in a visual review, survive two adversarial code reviewers, and get a human's nod before it's committed and the next one starts. Feedback from every review is remembered, so the loop gets more autonomous as the migration progresses.

Helix rebuilding a screen in the Shopify mobile app using Swift and Kotlin

This approach has been working extremely well and is allowing us to rebuild our apps in a fraction of the time.

Agentic control of simulators has been a bottleneck. We found ourselves constantly babysitting them as they couldn’t reliably build, test, and iterate. We built tooling to allow agents to reproduce bugs, fix them, and verify the fix autonomously but it was slow and brittle. React Native’s hot module reload helps the situation but it doesn’t solve it, due to simulator control being slow. This is primarily due to reliance on the accessibility tree, or screenshots to get the state of the app, take actions, and verify results. Agents can make code changes in seconds, but it takes them several minutes to test the output. This makes iterating extremely slow and manual. It doesn’t matter how good the model is if it can’t test its work quickly, which is especially difficult on mobile.

We’re fixing this by designing our app architecture to work for both humans and agents. The core principle here is that business logic should be completely decoupled from the UI and be able to run headlessly on desktop. We then make it available to agents via a CLI that allows them to iterate on it in milliseconds instead of minutes without involving simulators.

Navigating the app and performing actions using the CLI

The CLI allows agents to inspect the state of the app, navigate between different sections, and perform actions all without needing to touch the UI. This enables extremely fast feedback loops and allows agents to work autonomously for hours at a time.

When simulator interaction is needed, the CLI can connect to them via a remote mode and drive the UI via commands without having to inspect the layout or the accessibility tree. This enables blazing-fast performance and E2E tests.

This is real-time (not sped up)

We are going to migrate all our mobile apps to Swift and Kotlin using AI throughout the process. Shop has already shipped as a fully native app, the Shopify app is underway, and the rest will follow soon. We’re moving quickly, but not by lowering the bar. Every rebuild must meet or exceed the performance, stability, accessibility, and product quality people expect today. This isn’t just the same apps rewritten in different languages. We’re rebuilding them so both humans and agents can understand, test, and change them quickly.

The migration isn’t the finish line. Success means our teams can deliver better experiences for merchants and buyers faster than before. We’ll measure that through product velocity, app quality, and how much work agents can complete autonomously.

We’ll share what we learn along the way, including deeper dives into Helix, our agent-addressable architecture, and how we’re building mobile apps with agents. We were open about what we learned from React Native, and we intend to be just as open about this transition.

This is one of the most ambitious mobile engineering projects we’ve taken on. If you want to help build the next generation of Shopify’s mobile apps, we’re hiring mobile engineers, infrastructure engineers, and developers working at the intersection of AI and software engineering.

Native is the right choice for Shopify now, but React Native was the right choice for Shopify in 2020. That success was only possible because of the people who made it work.

Thank you to the React Native team at Meta for being excellent stewards of the framework, listening to our feedback, and working closely with us over the years. React Native is substantially better today because of your investments in its architecture, performance, tooling, and community.

Thank you for creating React Native Skia and taking it much further than any of us imagined. You redefined what was possible for graphics and animation in React Native, and we’re excited to see where you take it next.

Thank you for all your work on Reanimated, for listening to our feedback, and for helping us solve some of the hardest animation and performance problems in our apps.

Hundreds of engineers contributed to adopting React Native, migrating our apps, building shared foundations, improving performance, maintaining integrations, and contributing back to the ecosystem. Many of you became beginners again, challenged long-held assumptions, and made the transition successful while continuing to ship for merchants and buyers. Thank you.

Thank you to everyone who used our open-source libraries, contributed code, reported issues, challenged our decisions, and shared what you learned. Your contributions and feedback, including the spicy kind, made our work better.

The tools, lessons, and relationships built over the past six years will continue to shape how we build mobile apps at Shopify. We’re deeply grateful to everyone who was part of it.

See our open roles and learn more about our digital by design culture.
aiStories.fullTranslation:
编码智能体（Coding agents）改变了在两个平台上重复开发移动应用的成本。以下是 Shopify 为何从 React Native 迁回 Swift 和 Kotlin 的原因。

Shopify 工程团队
早在 2020 年，我们便决定全力投入 React Native，事实证明那次押注极为成功。我们只开发一次功能便节省了大量时间，让没有移动端背景的开发者也能为我们的应用贡献代码，并且不再需要疲于奔命地追求各平台功能对齐。

2025 年 1 月，我曾写道 React Native 前景光明，Shopify 计划继续对其进行投资。基于我们当时的认知，这完全属实。React Native 当时对我们来说运作良好，而且它至今仍是一个出色的框架。但自那时起，代码生成模型的性能取得了突破性提升，对于我们的应用和团队而言，分别用 Swift 和 Kotlin 构建同一功能已不再需要承担以往的高昂成本。

我们不会仅仅因为某项决定在过去取得过成功就固守不放。当核心假设发生变化时，我们愿意回过头来审视这是否依然是正确的选择。大语言模型（LLM）颠覆了支撑我们 2020 年决定的核心假设之一，因此我们从第一性原理重新评估了我们的移动端技术栈。

我们的评估结果指引我们回归原生开发。

我们在 2020 年决定从原生转向 React Native，主要是出于三个原因：
React Native 持续兑现了这些优势。我们发现自己花费了大量的时间和资源来优化性能、改进 React Native 的关键基础架构领域，并跟进框架更新和外部依赖项，但这些都是可以接受的权衡。使用 React Native 带来的收益，远远超过了我们在这些领域必须投入的成本。

Shopify 自 2021 年起（比 ChatGPT 面世还要早一年！）就已开始使用 LLM 来构建软件。起初，我们利用它们来实现具体功能、排查和修复缺陷，以及审查代码。随着模型性能的提升，我们放心交付给它们负责的工作复杂度也水涨船高。到了 2025 年底，它们已不仅仅是帮助我们更快地编写代码，更是让我们开始反思：在两个平台上分别构建软件，是否还等同于要做两倍的工作量。

我们决定重新评估移动技术栈，并着手制作原型，以检验以往的技术选型是否依然站得住脚。我们在 LLM 的辅助下，使用 Swift 和 Kotlin 重建了旗下最大型应用的几个核心模块，其运行成效令人惊叹。智能体：
原生开发仍意味着需要在两个平台上分别构建和维护软件，这部分成本并没有消失。发生改变的是，智能体现在已经能够承担足够多的实现、转译、测试和审查工作，以至于这不再是像 2020 年那样起决定性作用的考量因素。

React Native 应用可以做到运行飞快。我们的应用就很流畅。我们做出这一改变的原因在于，智能体削弱了共享代码实现所带来的优势，而为每个平台单独构建的优势依然存在。原生开发使我们能够更贴近平台特有能力和第一方工具链，在我们的代码与底层系统之间减少了框架层和依赖层。

在深入讨论我们具体如何迁移之前，我们希望确保这一过渡过程平稳妥善。自始至终，我们都希望回馈 React Native 生态使其更完善。我们发布过多个开源库，它们已经成为各自领域的首选方案。我们对社区给予的极高认可深表感激，并致力于确保这次过渡顺畅无阻、不带来任何意外困扰。

Shopify 将继续赞助该项目直至 2026 年底，William Candillon 在此之后也将继续投入该项目。他将在未来数月内复刻（fork）该代码仓，并开始以全新名称发布该库。在本次过渡完成后，原始仓库将被归档。我们将在这一过程中发布最新进展，以便大家有充裕的时间进行迁移。如果您的应用依赖该库，请考虑对其进行赞助。

该库每周下载量约达 200 万次，已成为 React Native 中渲染高性能列表的默认标准。鉴于其对整个生态系统的重要性，Shopify 将继续修复破坏兼容性的严重问题。我们目前正与数家公司接洽，商讨由谁长期接管 FlashList 的维护工作。若您有意承接，请在此与我联系。

Restyle 的用户群体较我们的其他开源库更小，因此我们正准备将此仓库归档。我们将维护其正常运行至 2026 年底，随后停止维护。欢迎任何人对其进行复刻并继续维护，如果有团队愿意接手，我们将全力协助交接工作。

Shopify 拥有多款大型应用（Shopify、Shop、Point of Sale、Inbox）。全球数以百万计的商家和买家每天都依赖这些应用谋生，并从他们喜爱的品牌购买所需商品。

我们曾权衡过是逐步迁移至原生（棕地迁移，brownfield）还是从零开始重构（绿地重构，greenfield）。过去当我们向 React Native 迁移时，对于部分最大的应用采取了棕地迁移策略，因为完全重写需要数年时间，且在重写期间我们不得不暂停交付新功能。

然而这一次，基于以下原因，从零开始的绿地重构脱颖而出成为明智之选：
在应用商店购物类榜单中常年名列前茅的 Shop 应用成为了首个迁移对象。在人工智能的辅助下，团队仅用 12 周时间，就完成了从概念验证到在应用商店上架全新原生重构应用的全过程。我们在此详细撰文介绍了这次迁移历程。

Shopify 应用（我们规模最大的应用，拥有 300 多个页面、主屏幕和锁屏小组件、Apple Watch 应用、复杂表盘功能、Siri 快捷指令等）的迁移工作也正在紧锣密鼓地推进中，将于今年晚些时候发布。我们其余的应用也将在不久后完成迁移。

直接把 LLM 指向 React Native 代码库，并试图“一步到位”生成原生版本的相同功能，这种做法极具诱惑力，但它根本行不通。即便你让模型预先收集尽可能多的信息，并将其固化为技术规范和任务文件后再去实现，你最终也会得到堆积如山、无法维护且根本无法交付上线的劣质代码。

为了解决这一难题，我们构建了一个名为 Helix 的系统，采取更为循序渐进的方式。它并不指望第一遍输出就完全正确，而是建立了一个反馈循环，任何有瑕疵的尝试在被修正为合格结果之前，绝对无法推进到下一步。

开发者将 Helix 指向某个具体页面。Helix 读取 React Native 代码，并提出一系列检查点（由小颗粒度、按顺序拆分的工作切片组成），几分钟内即可完成评审。随后，它逐个检查点推进构建：每一个检查点都必须通过测试验证其行为、在可视化审查中与运行中的应用表现一致、经受住两个对抗性代码审查智能体的挑剔，并获得人工开发者的认可，才能被提交并开始下一个切片。每一次审查的反馈都会被系统记录下来，因此随着迁移的推进，这个反馈循环的自主化程度也越来越高。

Helix 正在使用 Swift 和 Kotlin 重建 Shopify 移动应用中的一个页面

这种方法效果非常出色，让我们能够以极短的时间重构我们的应用程序。

智能体（Agent）对模拟器的控制一直是一个瓶颈。我们发现自己不得不时刻盯守着它们，因为它们无法可靠地进行构建、测试和迭代。我们构建了工具让智能体能够自主重现错误、修复错误并验证修复结果，但这既缓慢又脆弱。React Native 的模块热替换（hot module reload）有所帮助，但并不能根本解决问题，因为模拟器控制本身速度就很慢。这主要是因为需要依赖无障碍树（accessibility tree）或屏幕截图来获取应用状态、执行操作并验证结果。智能体可以在几秒钟内完成代码更改，但测试输出却需要几分钟。这使得迭代极其缓慢且依赖人工介入。如果模型无法快速测试其工作，那么模型本身有多优秀都无济于事，而这在移动端尤为困难。

我们正在通过设计同时适用于人类与智能体的应用架构来解决这一问题。这里的核心原则是业务逻辑应与 UI 完全解耦，并能够在桌面端无头（headless）运行。随后，我们通过命令行界面（CLI）将其提供给智能体，使它们能够在毫秒级别而非数分钟内对其进行迭代，且无需涉及模拟器。

使用 CLI 导航应用并执行操作

CLI 允许智能体检查应用状态、在不同板块之间导航以及执行操作，所有这一切都无需触碰 UI。这实现了极快的信息反馈回路，并允许智能体一次自主工作数小时。

当确实需要与模拟器交互时，CLI 可以通过远程模式连接到模拟器，并通过命令驱动 UI，而无需检查布局或无障碍树。这带来了极快的性能表现和端到端（E2E）测试能力。

这是实时的（未经过加速）

我们打算在整个过程中利用人工智能，将所有移动应用迁移到 Swift 和 Kotlin。Shop 已经作为完全的原生应用上线，Shopify 应用的迁移正在进行中，其余应用也将很快跟进。我们正在快速推进，但绝不降低标准。每一次重构都必须达到或超越人们如今所期待的性能、稳定性、无障碍性和产品质量。这不仅仅是用不同语言重写相同的应用。我们重构它们是为了让无论人类还是智能体都能快速理解、测试和修改它们。

迁移并不是终点线。成功意味着我们的团队能够比以往更快地为商家和买家提供更好的体验。我们将通过产品研发速度、应用质量以及智能体能够自主完成的工作量来衡量这一点。

我们将在推进过程中分享我们学到的经验，包括深入剖析我们面向智能体寻址的架构 Helix，以及我们如何与智能体协同构建移动应用。我们曾坦诚分享从 React Native 中吸取的经验教训，而对于这次转型，我们也打算同样保持开放。

这是我们开展过的最雄心勃勃的移动工程项目之一。如果你想帮助构建 Shopify 的下一代移动应用程序，我们正在招聘移动工程师、基础架构工程师以及在人工智能与软件工程交叉领域工作的开发者。

原生开发现在是 Shopify 的正确选择，但 React Native 则是 2020 年 Shopify 的正确选择。那一成功唯有依靠让其成为现实的人们才得以实现。

感谢 Meta 的 React Native 团队，你们一直是该框架卓越的管理者，倾听我们的反馈，并在这些年里与我们紧密合作。正是因为你们在其架构、性能、工具链和社区上的投入，React Native 如今才变得大为改观。

感谢你们打造了 React Native Skia，并将其推进到了远超我们所有人想象的高度。你们重新定义了 React Native 中图形和动画的可能性，我们非常期待看到你们未来将其带向何方。

感谢你们在 Reanimated 上的所有工作，感谢倾听我们的反馈，并帮助我们解决了应用中一些最棘手的动画和性能难题。

成百上千名工程师为采用 React Native、迁移我们的应用、构建共享基础、提升性能、维护集成以及向生态系统回馈贡献了力量。你们中的许多人重新变成了初学者，挑战长期存在的假设，并在继续为商家和买家交付产品的同时成功实现了转型。谢谢你们。

感谢所有使用我们的开源库、贡献代码、报告问题、质疑我们的决策并分享所学经验的人。你们的贡献和反馈，包括那些尖锐的批评，都让我们的工作变得更好。

过去六年中建立的工具、经验和人际纽带将继续塑造 Shopify 构建移动应用的方式。我们向每一位参与其中的人致以由衷的感谢。

How does Apple’s first folding phone stack up against the competition?

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

See All by Brad Bourque

Apple’s foldable phone is finally here — well, almost. The iPhone Duo, coming October 23rd, follows in the footsteps of past folding devices from Android phone makers like Samsung, OnePlus, and Google, with a $1,999 price tag that sits just above the Pixel 11 Pro Fold and Galaxy Z Fold 8.

While its hardware bears similarities to its competitors, the iPhone Duo is one of a few models that takes a passport-like approach. The aspect ratio is the same on the inside and outside screens, and it’s even usable with some apps while partially folded. The interior screen has a special outer layer, which along with its hinge design, makes the interior crease almost impossible to spot (something that many competitors struggle to do, though Samsung and Oppo are making fantastic progress).

We got a chance to spend some time with the iPhone Duo at Apple’s “Surprise and shine” event, so our hands-on is a great place to start if you want to learn more about how it actually feels to use. We’ll be continuing to cover the phone as we get closer to launch, so make sure to stay tuned for our full review down the road.

Comparing specs between foldables from Apple and Android makers isn’t always one-to-one, just like comparing slab-style phones. However, we think it’s still useful to present all the specs from the iPhone Duo’s most similar competitors.

aiStories.fullContent:
Posts from this topic will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Chasing unrealistic standards encourages men to turn themselves into DIY science experiments.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

See All by Victoria Song

Whenever the algorithm serves up a steaming pile of looksmaxxing, I flash back to an old sketch from That Mitchell and Webb Look. An ordinary woman is told by a commercial narrator that she’s “leaking, hairy, aging, overweight, and everything hurts.” Women, the smug narrator says, for god’s sake, sort yourselves out by buying roughly $300 of products. After a jump cut, an average man is told to shave and get drunk, guitars blaring in the background. The reason? Because he’s already brilliant.

Back when that sketch first aired in 2009, it was funny because it felt broadly true. But in the age of looksmaxxing, where men are increasingly obsessed with testosterone, smashing their bones in pursuit of a sharp jawline, and optimizing their penises, that sketch feels like a glimpse into antiquity.

Today, you have men in subreddits and Facebook groups posting before-and-after pics at the gym, arms flexed for maximum veiny bicep effect. In the comments, they ask for each other’s stacks, protocols, and dosing advice, which include everything from T to unapproved gray-market peptides. Some say it’s to score baddies. Others say it’s to maximize their gains at the gym. A few seem to think turning themselves into science experiments is how they’ll find the fountain of youth. To me, it feels similar to what women have done for ages: buying snake oil that preys on their insecurities.

“I take Cialis, but not for sex,” begins one of biohacker and tech entrepreneur Bryan Johnson’s X posts. “It’s actually a longevity medicine. Cialis (Tadalafil) is great for the same reason it gives you fantastic erections… it improves blood flow.”

Tadalafil does, in fact, improve blood flow. The medicine is a vasodilator, meaning it relaxes muscles and widens blood vessels. It’s most widely known as a treatment for erectile dysfunction. (To be clear, it doesn’t cause erections but helps them last when they occur.) It’s also prescribed to alleviate urinary issues in people with enlarged prostates and high blood pressure in the pulmonary artery. Biohackers like Johnson tout a low dose of tadalafil daily as helping lower cardiovascular risk and cognitive decline. Gym rats often microdose tadalafil as a preworkout supplement because, well, the erections are supposedly better and dilating blood vessels is thought to lead to better “muscle pumps.”

Enhanced, the company behind the pro-doping Enhanced Games, sells low-dose tadalafil on its site. Clavicular, the most infamous looksmaxxer, has also stated that he’s taken about 5mg of tadalafil in the past as part of an extensive stack. This, despite the fact that he’s 20 years old and far from the conventional profile of someone a doctor might prescribe tadalafil to. Popular podcaster Andrew Huberman has also recommended on his show that every man over 40 should be taking a low dose of tadalafil as a preventative measure.

Of course, tadalafil is just like any other medicine. While many may not experience adverse effects at low daily dosages, some will. And like any medication, there are some people who shouldn’t take it and there are drug interactions to be wary of.

It’d be one thing if these influencers were just promoting tadalafil. But most are promoting multiple substances, seemingly all of which you need to be a man. Testosterone, for instance, is massively popular in the same cohort. Ninety-one percent of the athletes at the inaugural Enhanced Games dabbled with testosterone. Notably, Pete Hegseth recently announced mandatory testosterone screenings for the troops. Some also hype up retatrutide, an unapproved peptide currently undergoing phase three clinical trials, along with TB-500 and BPC-157, two gray-market peptides colloquially known as the Wolverine stack for their supposed wound healing and muscle recovery benefits. And the more things you stack, the greater the risk that a combination has an unintended effect. In the case of lesser-studied experimental treatments, even doctors may not know what those effects are — and might not know for a long time.

The stated reasons for taking these risks are myriad. But whether it’s because it’ll help someone get jacked, live longer, perform better in bed, or just “have more energy,” it boils down to a singular message: It’ll make you more of a man.

“This kind of masculinity is a little bit fantastical,” says Dr. Arthur Burnett, the Patrick C. Walsh professor of urology at Johns Hopkins, referring to the current cultural obsession with “maxxing.” Burnett should know. On top of over three decades as a men’s health expert, his research into nitric oxide biochemical mechanisms in erectile tissue helped pave the way for drugs like Viagra.

Regarding men taking on all of these additional requirements, he says that “there’s not really a scientific basis.”“I think it’s unfortunate that we’ve pushed the pendulum in a direction that may be harmful, frankly, psychologically at the very least but possibly even physically to the body. It could be problematic trying to adopt medical terms like ‘prevention’ and ‘men’s health’.”

I’m researching a story on peptide use, and I’m looking to interview regular people who are using gray-market peptides. If you’re interested in participating, email me at victoria.song@theverge.com or message me at Signal @vicmsong.14.

Burnett is essentially pointing to the divide between how clinicians and the biohacking / looksmaxxing communities view medicine. On the one side, you have medical professionals who largely view drugs as a way to treat deficiencies and bring people back to a “normal” baseline. On the other, you have influencers and enthusiasts (which can include clinicians) who believe that drugs can and ought to be used to “enhance” people beyond their natural limits. It’s a tension that’s at the heart of so many debates in the wellness wild west.

“Preventative care should really be something that those who are at risk or have health adversities can make changes in a way that’s going to correct a problem. What you have here is completely healthy people doing things that can be problematic,” explains Burnett.

Testosterone, he says, is a classic example. Otherwise healthy men who over-supplement the hormonal steroid often inadvertently make themselves infertile. For some men, too much testosterone can also trigger a genetic predisposition for hair thinning — which looksmaxxers often address by taking minoxidil. Add another supplement, drug, or product to combat the side effects of minoxidil — which include dizziness, headaches, and bloating — and that’s how you end up with a stack.

What gets lost in all these stacks and protocols is that health isn’t about optimization. For many young men, “optimizing” seems to be less of a goal than a vaguely defined baseline they’re expected to maintain forever. Anything less is a failure, a weakness — unhealthy.

A depressing way to spend an afternoon is rifling through looksmaxxing and gear forums. (I don’t recommend staying too long — unless you feel like torturing yourself reading 4chan-esque insults and slurs about penis size and “weekly slays.”)

In one post, a supposed 18-year-old asks for advice dosing Cialis to have better erections and “get more flaccid hang.” In a biohacking subreddit, a 30-year-old essentially crowdsources whether he’s developing a “dependency” on tadalafil. At no point, despite all the posturing, do any of the men in the posts I read seem to be genuinely happy. They’re often boastful about how good they feel or how many conquests they’ve had. But mostly, there seems to be an undercurrent of angry self-loathing. A desperate urge to “fix” oneself for… what or whom exactly? I never find a coherent answer.

Admittedly, I’m not a man. I will never know what it means to be a man or experience the societal pressures that men face. But there’s something strange about how the internet is amplifying a subsect of men turning themselves into science experiments. There’s a veritable pipeline from relatively benign trends like boy kibble protein-washing and news stories about RFK Jr. working out shirtless with Kid Rock to whatever it is the Enhanced Games and Bryan Johnson are doing. It’s easy to write off, until Whoop’s AI recommends your boss up his testosterone levels — not because he’s deficient, but because he’s not optimized for performance.

“It happens in my clinic periodically — guys thinking they need enhancements, or they’re unhappy with certain interventions, or they feel they’re not performing at a certain level,” says Burnett. “It’s counterproductive as it actually promotes stigma [around men’s health] because they can’t live up to what they think is the notion of the ideal man.” That, he says, creates more anxiety, stress, embarrassment, and shame. On top of that, it makes it hard for men to speak more openly about genuine health issues or seek a professional’s help. Anything “abnormal” becomes something to be suffered in silence or supplemented away.

For now, it’s probably contained to a chronically online niche. (Burnett says these behaviors aren’t heavily prevalent in his practice just yet, but then again — how likely are the most susceptible men to trust the medical establishment when that’s the first thing wellness grifters seek to discredit?) But this niche is loud and it loves to post. Eventually, those messages embed themselves in the broader culture — even if everyone knows better.

The only thing I can conclude is that the looksmaxxers are not okay. I hope that one day they will be, that this is a passing fad that one day we’ll look back and laugh at. But in the meantime, I’ll leave this with some advice from Burnett.

“As long as we’re living healthy, we’re doing the right thing. Please accept that you are a good man for who you are, and don’t be swayed by the influencers.”

追逐不切实际的标准正在促使男性把自己变成DIY科学实验品。
来自该作者的帖子将被添加到您的每日电子邮件文摘和主页信息流中。
查看维多利亚·宋（Victoria Song）的全部文章
每当算法推送一大堆“颜值最大化”（looksmaxxing）的内容时，我脑海中就会浮现出英剧《米切尔和韦伯秀》（That Mitchell and Webb Look）中的一段老小品。在短剧里，一位普通的女性被广告旁白告知，她“身体漏液、体毛旺盛、衰老、超重，而且浑身哪都疼”。那位自以为是的旁白说，女人们看在上帝的分上，赶紧买上大约300美元的产品来收拾好自己吧。镜头一转，切到了一个普通男性身上，旁白伴随着刺耳的吉他背景乐告诉他去刮个胡子喝个烂醉就行。原因何在？因为他本来就已经足够优秀了。
早在2009年该小品首次播出时，它之所以搞笑，是因为它在很大程度上让人觉得很真实。但在“颜值最大化”的时代——男性越来越痴迷于睾酮、为了追求刀削般的下颌线而砸击自己的骨头、并试图优化自己的阴茎——那段小品如今看起来就像是遥远古代的浮光掠影。
如今，你会看到男人们在Reddit子版块和Facebook群组里发布自己在健身房的前后对比照，紧绷双臂以展现最具血管凸显感的二头肌效果。在评论区，他们互相打听彼此的药物搭配方案（stacks）、用药协议和剂量建议，其中涵盖了从睾酮（T）到未经批准的灰色市场多肽类药物等各种成分。有人说这是为了泡辣妹。也有人说这是为了在健身房实现增肌效益最大化。还有少数人似乎认为，把自己变成科学实验品就能找到青春之泉。在我看来，这与女性长久以来的遭遇如出一辙：购买利用她们的不安全感大发横财的“万灵假药”。
“我吃希爱力（Cialis），但不是为了啪啪啪，”生物黑客兼科技创业者布莱恩·约翰逊（Bryan Johnson）在X平台的一篇帖子开篇写道。“它其实是一种长寿药。希爱力（他达拉非）之所以棒，原因正如它能给你带来绝佳的勃起一样……它能改善血流。”
事实上，他达拉非确实能够改善血流。该药物是一种血管舒张剂，这意味着它能放松肌肉并扩张血管。它最广为人知的用途是治疗勃起功能障碍。（需要明确的是，它本身不会引发勃起，但能在勃起发生时帮助其持续。）它也被开具用于缓解前列腺肥大患者的排尿问题以及治疗肺动脉高压。像约翰逊这样的生物黑客吹嘘每天小剂量服用他达拉非有助于降低心血管疾病风险和认知能力下降。健身爱好者们经常将他达拉非微量用作练前补剂，因为怎么说呢，据说勃起状态会更好，而且扩张血管被认为能带来更好的“肌肉泵感”。
支持使用兴奋剂的“增强运动会”（Enhanced Games）背后的公司Enhanced，就在其官网上销售低剂量的他达拉非。最声名狼藉的“颜值最大化”拥趸Clavicular也曾表示，他过去曾服用约5毫克的他达拉非作为其庞大用药方案的一部分。然而，他年仅20岁，与医生通常会为其开具他达拉非的人群特征相去甚远。知名播客主持人安德鲁·胡伯曼（Andrew Huberman）也在其节目中建议，每位40岁以上的男性都应小剂量服用他达拉非作为一种预防措施。
当然，他达拉非和其他任何药物并无二致。虽然许多人在每日低剂量下可能不会出现不良反应，但仍有一部分人会出现副作用。并且正如任何药物一样，有些人是不应服用它的，同时还需要警惕药物相互作用。
如果这些网红只是在推销他达拉非，那倒也罢了。但绝大多数人都在推销多种物质，而且看起来每一种都是为了“成为真男人”所必需的。例如，睾酮在同一群体中极度流行。首届增强运动会中有91%的运动员涉足过睾酮。值得注意的是，皮特·赫格塞斯（Pete Hegseth）最近宣布对军队进行强制性睾酮筛查。还有人吹捧替尔泊肽类似物retatrutide（一种未经批准、目前正在进行三期临床试验的多肽药物），以及TB-500和BPC-157——这两种灰色市场的多肽药物因被认为具有伤口愈合和肌肉恢复功效而通称为“金刚狼方案”（Wolverine stack）。而你叠加使用的药物越多，组合产生非预期效应的风险就越大。在研究较少的实验性疗法中，甚至连医生都可能不知道这些影响是什么——而且可能很长一段时间内都不会知晓。
冒这些风险的明面理由数不胜数。但无论是为了帮助某人练就强壮体魄、活得更久、在床上表现更佳，还是仅仅为了“拥有更多精力”，归根结底都传递着一个单一的信息：它会让你更有男子气概。
“这种男性气概带有一点幻想色彩，”约翰斯·霍普金斯大学帕特里克·C·沃尔什泌尿学教授阿瑟·伯内特博士（Dr. Arthur Burnett）在谈及当前文化对“最大化（maxxing）”的痴迷时说道。伯内特对此再清楚不过了。除了作为男性健康专家深耕三十余年外，他对勃起组织中一氧化氮生化机制的研究，曾为伟哥等药物的问世奠定了基础。
针对男性承担所有这些额外要求，他表示“实际上并没有科学依据”。“我认为，不幸的是，我们已经把钟摆推向了一个可能有害的方向，坦率地讲，至少在心理上是有害的，甚至可能在身体上也产生危害。试图套用‘预防’和‘男性健康’等医学术语可能会带来问题。”
我正在就多肽药物的使用展开专题调查报道，并希望采访正在使用灰色市场多肽药物的普通人。如果您有兴趣参与，请发送电子邮件至 victoria.song@theverge.com 或通过 Signal 发送消息至 @vicmsong.14。
伯内特实质上指出了临床医生与生物黑客/“颜值最大化”群体在看待药物方面的分歧。一方面，医疗专业人士主要将药物视为治疗身体机能缺陷、使人恢复到“正常”基线的一种手段。另一方面，网红和发烧友们（其中也可以包括部分临床医生）则认为，药物可以而且应当被用来“增强”人体，使其超越自然极限。这种紧张关系正是这片肆意蔓延的养生保健蛮荒之地中诸多争论的核心所在。
“预防性医疗应当是让那些面临健康风险或遭遇健康逆境的人能够做出改变，以纠正问题。而眼下的情况是，完全健康的人正在做着可能带来麻烦的事情，”伯内特解释道。
他说，睾酮就是一个典型的例子。其他方面健康的男性如果过度补充这种类固醇激素，往往会在无意中导致自己不育。对某些男性而言，过多的睾酮还会诱发脱发的遗传倾向——而“颜值最大化”追随者往往通过服用米诺地尔来应对这种脱发。然后再添加另一种补剂、药物或产品来对抗米诺地尔的副作用（包括头晕、头痛和腹胀）——这就是人们最终搞出一整套药物搭配方案的全过程。

在所有这些补剂组合与严苛方案中被遗忘的是：健康并不等同于极致优化。对于许多年轻男性而言，“优化”似乎不再是一个追求的目标，而更像是一条被期望永久保持的、定义模糊的基准线。任何达不到这一标准的表现都会被视为失败、软弱，即不健康。

虚度整个下午的一种令人沮丧的方式，就是翻阅外貌最大化（looksmaxxing）和违禁药物（gear）论坛。（我并不建议在里面待太久——除非你想自讨苦吃，去读那些充满 4chan 风格的侮辱言辞、关于阴茎尺寸的谩骂以及所谓的“每周战绩”）。

在一则帖子中，一名据称18岁的年轻人发帖求助希爱力（Cialis）的用药剂量，以期获得更好的勃起硬度和“更显修长的疲软状态”。在一个生物黑客 Reddit 版块中，一名30岁的男子实际上是在向网友众包咨询，确认自己是否正在对达泊拉非（tadalafil）产生“依赖”。尽管姿态做尽，但在我读过的所有帖子里，没有哪一个男人看起来是真正快乐的。他们常常吹嘘自己感觉有多棒，或者炫耀自己有多少性征服经历。但大多数时候，字里行间涌动着一股愤怒的自我厌恶暗流。那种迫切想要“修整”自己的冲动，究竟是为了……什么，抑或是为了谁？我从未找到过一个说得通的答案。

诚然，我不是男人。我永远无法体会身为男人意味着什么，也无法经历男性所面对的社会压力。然而，互联网正在放大某一部分把自己当作科学实验品的男性群体，这一现象着实透着诡异。从相对无害的趋势（如将“单身汉简餐”进行蛋白质概念包装），到小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪（RFK Jr.）与摇滚小子（Kid Rock）光着膀子健身的新闻，再到“增强运动会”（Enhanced Games）和布莱恩·约翰逊（Bryan Johnson）所搞的一切，这之间存在着一条切实的发展链条。人们很容易对此一笑置之，直到 Whoop 的 AI 建议你的老板提高睾酮水平——不是因为他缺乏睾酮，而是因为他在体能表现上尚未达到“最佳优化状态”。

“在我的门诊中时常发生这种情况——有些人认为自己需要强化手段，或者对某些干预措施感到不满，又或者觉得自己未能在特定层面上表现达标，”伯内特（Burnett）说。“这其实适得其反，因为它助长了（围绕男性健康的）污名化，因为他们无法企及自己心目中所设想的理想男人标准。”他说，这会引发更多的焦虑、压力、尴尬和羞耻感。最重要的是，这让男性很难坦诚地谈论真正的健康问题或向专业人士求助。任何“不正常”的现象，都变成了要么默默忍受、要么靠补剂强行压制的问题。

目前而言，这种现象或许还局限在那些重度网瘾的小众群体中。（伯内特表示，这类行为在他的诊所里还没有普遍流行，但话又说回来——那些最易受影响的男性，怎么可能去信任医疗机构呢？毕竟养生骗子们首先要诋毁的就是正规医疗体系。）然而这个小群体声音极大，并且热衷于发帖。最终，哪怕大家都心知肚明，这些观念还是会渗透到更广泛的文化中。

我唯一能得出的结论是：这些外貌最大化者（looksmaxxers）的心理状态并不健康。我希望有朝一日他们能好起来，希望这只是一阵过眼云烟的狂热潮流，未来某一天我们可以回过头来付之一笑。但在此期间，我愿以伯内特的一段建议作为结语：

“只要我们健康地生活，就是在做正确的事情。请接纳真实的自己就是一个优秀的男人，不要被那些网红牵着鼻子走。”

aiStories.title: 谷歌与印度初创公司Mitti Labs签署其最大水稻甲烷碳信用交易
aiStories.originalTitle: Google signs its biggest rice-methane carbon credit deal with Indian startup Mitti Labs
aiStories.snippet: The four-year agreement will cover rice farms across three Indian states, reaching about 100,000 hectares at peak delivery.
aiStories.fullContent:
Google has agreed to buy 1 million carbon credits from Indian climate-tech startup Mitti Labs through 2030, in what the companies say is the largest publicly announced deal to date for credits generated from cutting methane emissions in rice farming.

The four-year agreement will cover rice farms across the Indian states of Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, and Telangana, reaching about 100,000 hectares at peak delivery, Mitti Labs co-founder Xavier Laguarta said in an interview. Financial terms were not disclosed.

The project will pay farmers to adopt practices that reduce how long rice fields remain flooded, cutting methane released during cultivation while also reducing water use. Mitti Labs says the technique can cut methane emissions by about 50% and irrigation water use by about 40% without reducing crop yields.

The deal comes as Google faces the challenge of reaching its goal of going net-zero emissions by 2030 amid investing heavily in artificial-intelligence infrastructure. Its greenhouse gas emissions in 2025 grew 18% year-over-year to about 14.5 million metric tons of carbon dioxide equivalent, per its environmental report (PDF) released in June.

Mitti Labs began talks with Google about a year ago, Laguarta told TechCrunch, as the tech company explored adding methane-reduction projects to its carbon-credit portfolio. Google was drawn in part to the project’s water savings and Mitti Labs’ ability to operate at scale, he stated.

The startup’s projects have saved more than 500 billion liters of water over the past two years. The Google deal, Laguarta said, would allow Mitti Labs to expand further, giving it the scale needed to work with large corporate buyers.

“Having Google, one of the most sophisticated buyers in the market with rigorous due diligence processes, is obviously a good signal for us,” Laguarta said, adding that the deal would allow Mitti to scale significantly.

Google’s evaluation included scrutiny of Mitti Labs’ monitoring technology and visits to farms before the companies signed the agreement, Laguarta said. Founded in 2023, the New York- and Bengaluru-based startup has built a GeoAI platform that combines satellite radar imagery with field measurements to remotely track crop growth, soil moisture and flooding across smallholder farms.

The platform uses synthetic aperture radar imagery from commercial and public satellites, with resolutions ranging from 50 centimeters to 10 meters. Mitti also uses proprietary data collected in the field to train its AI models, Laguarta said.

The credits sold to Google can be issued under either Gold Standard or Isometric, two carbon-credit certification bodies, Laguarta said. He added that the projects undergo independent third-party verification as part of the certification process before credits are issued.

In addition to Google, Mitti Labs works with customers including carbon marketplace Cool Effect, rice producer Ebro Foods, and agricultural company Syngenta. Laguarta told TechCrunch that the Google agreement is Mitti Labs’ largest offtake deal to date.

Mitti Labs currently works with more than 100,000 farmers and aims to have millions of farmers by 2030. The Google deal, Laguarta said, would help the startup move toward that goal by allowing it to expand its projects.

A majority of the revenue from the startup’s projects goes to farming communities, Laguarta noted. He declined to disclose how much farmers participating in the Google project would receive, however.

While the Google project is limited to India, Mitti Labs plans to launch operations in the Philippines later this year and expand into Indonesia and other Southeast Asian markets in 2027.

Laguarta sees room for the market to grow as more companies look to agricultural projects to tackle methane emissions. About 150 million farmers grow rice across India, Southeast Asia, and China, he told TechCrunch.

The deal with Mitti Labs is not Google’s first carbon-removal investment in India. In January 2025, the Mountain View, California-headquartered company partnered with Gurugram-based Varaha to buy 100,000 tons of carbon credits. That was Google’s first large-scale purchase of carbon removal credits in the country and the largest involving biomass-produced biochar.

Google is also turning to clean-energy projects in India to address its supply-chain emissions. The company has signed an agreement tied to a 150-megawatt solar project in Rajasthan, taking its contracted solar capacity with ReNew in the state to 300 megawatts.

谷歌已同意在2030年前向印度气候科技初创公司Mitti Labs购买100万个碳信用额度。两家公司表示，这是迄今为止公开宣布的、通过减少水稻种植中甲烷排放产生的最大一笔碳信用交易。

Mitti Labs联合创始人哈维尔·拉瓜尔塔（Xavier Laguarta）在接受采访时表示，这项为期四年的协议将覆盖印度卡纳塔克邦、安得拉邦和特伦甘纳邦的水稻农田，在最高交付期将覆盖约10万公顷。具体财务条款未予披露。

该项目将向采用新实践的农民支付报酬，这些实践可以减少稻田被水淹没的时间，从而减少种植过程中释放的甲烷，同时也降低了用水量。Mitti Labs表示，该技术可以在不降低作物产量的情况下，减少约50%的甲烷排放，并减少约40%的灌溉用水。

这笔交易达成之际，正值谷歌在对人工智能基础设施进行大力投资的同时，面临着实现2030年净零排放目标的挑战。根据其6月发布的环境报告（PDF），谷歌2025年的温室气体排放量同比增长了18%，达到约1450万公吨二氧化碳当量。

拉瓜尔塔告诉TechCrunch，Mitti Labs在大约一年前开始与谷歌进行谈判，当时这家科技公司正在探索将其碳信用投资组合增加减少甲烷排放的项目。他表示，谷歌被吸引的部分原因是该项目的节水效果以及Mitti Labs规模化运营的能力。

在过去两年中，这家初创公司的项目已累计节约了超过5000亿升水。拉瓜尔塔表示，与谷歌的协议将使Mitti Labs能够进一步扩张，为其提供与大型企业买家合作所需的规模。

“让谷歌这样市场上最成熟、尽职调查流程最严格的买家之一加入进来，对我们来说显然是一个积极的信号，”拉瓜尔塔说，并补充称这笔交易将使Mitti得以大幅扩张。

拉瓜尔塔表示，在双方签署协议之前，谷歌的评估包括对Mitti Labs监测技术的严格审查以及对农场的实地考察。这家成立于2023年、总部设在纽约和班加罗尔的初创公司建立了一个地理人工智能（GeoAI）平台，该平台结合卫星雷达图像与实地测量，远程跟踪小农户农田的作物生长、土壤水分和水淹情况。

该平台使用来自商业和公共卫星的合成孔径雷达图像，分辨率在50厘米至10米之间。拉瓜尔塔表示，Mitti还利用在农田现场收集的专有数据来训练其人工智能模型。

拉瓜尔塔说，出售给谷歌的碳信用额度可以在Gold Standard或Isometric这两个碳信用认证机构之一下签发。他补充说，在签发信用额度之前，作为认证程序的一部分，这些项目会接受独立的第三方核查。

除谷歌外，Mitti Labs的客户还包括碳交易平台Cool Effect、大米生产商Ebro Foods以及农业公司先正达（Syngenta）。拉瓜尔塔告诉TechCrunch，与谷歌达成的协议是Mitti Labs迄今为止最大的承购协议。

Mitti Labs目前与超过10万名农民合作，并力争在2030年前吸引数百万农民加入。拉瓜尔塔表示，与谷歌的交易将允许该公司扩展其项目，从而有助于推动初创公司走向该目标。

拉瓜尔塔指出，该初创公司项目的大部分收入都会流向农业社区。不过，他拒绝透露参与谷歌项目的农民将获得多少报酬。

虽然谷歌的项目仅限于印度，但Mitti Labs计划于今年晚些时候在菲律宾启动业务，并在2027年进军印度尼西亚和其他东南亚市场。

拉瓜尔塔认为，随着越来越多企业寻求通过农业项目来应对甲烷排放，该市场有增长空间。他告诉TechCrunch，在印度、东南亚和中国，约有1.5亿农民种植水稻。

与Mitti Labs的交易并不是谷歌在印度的第一笔碳清除投资。2025年1月，这家总部位于加州山景城的公司与总部位于古尔冈的Varaha合作购买了10万吨碳信用。这是谷歌在印度进行的首次大规模碳清除信用采购，也是涉及生物质制生物炭的最大采购。

谷歌还在印度转向清洁能源项目，以解决其供应链排放问题。该公司已就拉贾斯坦邦的一个150兆瓦太阳能项目签署协议，使其在该邦与ReNew签约的太阳能容量达到300兆瓦。
